oneVps.name: One VPS
oneVps.desc: One app server and one database. Each request makes 3 queries, so the database runs out of CPU first, at about 167 req/s.

addCache.name: Add a cache
addCache.desc: 85% of reads now come from the cache, cutting database load by three quarters. The bottleneck moves to the app server's CPU.

scaleOut.name: Scale out
scaleOut.desc: A load balancer spreads traffic over 4 servers. The app tier can take 800 req/s, so the database is the limit again.

readReplicas.name: Read replicas
readReplicas.desc: Two replicas take the reads, but each still replays every write. With the primary only handling writes, the replicas become the limit.

blackFriday.name: Black Friday
blackFriday.desc: Traffic jumps 5×. Most requests fail. Try a CDN, more servers and more replicas to survive it.

async.name: Async
async.desc: Each worker juggles many requests at once (Node.js, FastAPI with async code).

sync.name: Sync
sync.desc: Each worker handles one request at a time (Gunicorn sync workers, PHP-FPM, Unicorn).

distributedSim.regionHint: Click a region to take it down; its traffic goes to the others.
distributedSim.stackNote: Every region runs a copy of part 1's Read replicas stack: async workers, 10 ms of CPU per request, 3 queries per request, 4 ms per query.
distributedSim.poolerNote: Workers connect to the pooler instead of the databases. It keeps a small pool of server connections to each one and queues queries until one is free.
distributedSim.retryBudgetHint: Retries capped at 10% of the real traffic.
distributedSim.sheddingHint: The load balancer rejects what exceeds the threshold instead of queueing it.
distributedSim.diagramLabel: Architecture diagram, one band per region. Click a component to inspect it, or a region's button to take it down.

warnings.failover: Region {from} is down, so the primaries have failed over to region {to}. Every other region's writes now cross to it.
warnings.connectionsExceeded: {regions} regions × {servers} servers × {workers} workers × {pool} connections = {needed} to each primary, but the database allows {max}. The extra connections are refused; a pooler fixes this.
warnings.hotShard: One shard takes {share} of the queries instead of an even {even}. Sharding only helps as far as the busiest shard allows; the other {shards} shards' capacity goes unused.
warnings.crossRegionReads: No replicas, so reads from all {regions} regions go to the primary's region and pay the round trip on every query.
warnings.retries: Retries add {retries} req/s, {extra}% on top of the real traffic, and get no more requests through once a component is saturated.
warnings.shedding: {shed} req/s are rejected at once by load shedding, so the admitted requests don't queue.

oneRegion.name: One region
oneRegion.desc: Part 1's Read replicas stack with a 4 vCPU database, in one region: 6 servers take up to 1,200 req/s. Every scenario here builds on it.

regionLoss.name: Region loss
regionLoss.desc: Three regions share 2,700 req/s at 75% each. Region 3 is down, so the other two get 1,350 req/s each, 12% more than they can take. Bring it back, or keep a region's worth of headroom.

crossRegion.name: Cross-region reads
crossRegion.desc: Three regions but no replicas, so every cache miss crosses 80 ms to the primary in region 1. The remote regions answer in 74 ms instead of 17 ms. Add a replica to keep reads local.

hotShard.name: Hot shard
hotShard.desc: Four shards, but 70% of the queries hit one of them. Its replica is at 99% while the other three sit at 14%, so the limit is 2,026 req/s instead of 5,674 with an even split.

retryStorm.name: Retry storm
retryStorm.desc: 8% more traffic than the app tier can take, and clients retry every failure 3 times. Attempts almost double, nothing more gets through, and the error rate is the same as with no retries.

shedding.name: Load shedding
shedding.desc: The same overload, but the load balancer rejects what exceeds 80% of capacity and retries stay within a 10% budget. 26% of requests fail fast, and the rest finish in 32 ms instead of timing out.
